entities.summary: Humbert of Romans, OP was a French Dominican friar who served as the fifth Master General of the Order of Preachers from 1254 to 1263. He played a significant role in the establishment of the Dominican Order in Europe, promoting the establishment of monasteries and the creation of a rigorous spiritual discipline. As Master General, he oversaw the expansion of the Order into England and Ireland, and worked to standardize the Order's practices and rituals. He also wrote several treatises on theology and spirituality, including a commentary on the works of St. Augustine. Humbert's legacy as a reformer and a spiritual guide continues to be felt within the Dominican Order and beyond. The exact date of his birth is unknown, but he died on July 21, 1277, at the age of 83. His contributions to the establishment of the Dominican Order and his writings on theology and spirituality have left a lasting impact on the development of Christian spirituality in Europe.
